newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft ahead of U.S. job figures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft ahead of U.S. job figures.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker across the board in thin trade due to demand for dollars by dealers who shunned stock market gains and instead looked ahead to U.S. employment figures being released on Friday, traders said.
"Trade has been slow because we're at the beginning of the month, but dealers are cautious too because of Friday's (U.S. employment) figures," a trader said.
Dealers feared that U.S. employment figures could push up U.S. long bond yields and weaken the peso.
The benchmark 48-hour and 24-hour peso slid throughout the session to close two and 1.3 centavos weaker, respectively to 7.5380/7.5410 7.5250/7.5300 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 0.3 of a centavo weaker at 7.5135/7.5160 per dollar.
Dealers noted that gains in share prices did not draw dollars into the foreign exchange market, as was the case on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"We didn't see any foreigners in the forex market. Those investing in the bolsa probably already had pesos," said a trader.
The leading IPC stock index was up 20.03 points, 0.60 percent, at 3,378.35 when the foreign exchange market closed.
Traders said they expected trade to pick up on Friday after the U.S. jobs data.
